summary: Validates output capacity via AddConstantWrapper, writes the resulting header word into the destination, copies a variable-length data block resolved by BufferQueryReturnPtrSizeIfValid, then appends three trailing struct fields (DWORD at 0x10, DWORD at 0x14, BYTE at 0x18). Returns the total written byte count through *a3.

local_names.v14: remaining destination size (decremented by the 2 header bytes)

operations.description: Call AddConstantWrapper(this) to obtain the value v4 used for the capacity check.
If v4 > *a3, the destination is too small; return 0 immediately.
Write v4 as a WORD header at the start of the destination buffer; set the write cursor to a2+2 and v14 = *a3 - 2.
Call BufferQueryReturnPtrSizeIfValid(&v15, &v14) to resolve the source pointer/size for the data block.
If the buffer query succeeds, copy 4*(v14>>2) bytes from the resolved source, then the remaining v14&3 bytes; advance the destination cursor by the full copied size.
Append the first trailing DWORD read from this+0x10 at the destination cursor.
Append the second trailing DWORD read from this+0x14 after the first trailing field.
Append the trailing BYTE read from this+0x18 after the two DWORD fields.
Store the total written size (final cursor minus start plus one) into *a3.

unresolved: Semantic meaning of the three trailing fields (two DWORDs + one BYTE) appended after the copied data block is unknown; they likely tag the decoded block but no consuming evidence is present.
Relationship between AddConstantWrapper's return value and the header word written to the destination is unclear (capacity versus data size).
The off-by-one in the reported size (*a3 = cursor - dst + 1) suggests a byte counting convention that is not explained by the packet.
